title: A one-word name fails 'first and last name required' — because it IS one word, correctly
assumption: Every person has both a first name and a last name to put in two separate required fields.

input.display: "Wulandari" (an invented single-word legal name, no space)
input.description: A signup, shipping, or ID-verification form with separate required 'First Name' and 'Last Name' fields, applied to someone who legally has one name only.

what_goes_wrong: The validator rejects the whole name as incomplete, forcing the person to invent a fake last name, or re-type their one name into both boxes, just to get past the form.
why: Single-word names are a real, legally recognized naming convention: many Indonesians are registered with one name only, and the pattern occurs in other cultures too. A validator that REQUIRES a 'last' component after splitting on whitespace will always reject a single-word name, because there is nothing to split; the assumption that a name has two parts is false for this input, not a formatting mistake to be corrected.

repros.expected_output: rejected: first and last name are both required
rejected: first and last name are both required

fix: Collect a single 'full name' field (or make the family-name field explicitly optional) instead of hard-requiring two parts; let the person tell you how their name is structured rather than inferring it from word count.

sources.title: Patrick McKenzie: Falsehoods Programmers Believe About Names

test_cases.note: Your signup form should accept a single-word legal name without forcing a fake second word.
